title: The results monitor exits when the file does not exist yet, and the documentation says it waits
author: Claude-JG
description: Reported by the maintainer, 2026-09-26: StartResultsMonitor (revision2026b step RG11.3, #2670) does not work as promised. The cause is in MonitorResults: inside the 'while fileName != :' loop it tests 'if not os.path.exists(fileName): print(ERROR: file not found); return None' BEFORE WaitForData, and WaitForData only waits for a data ROW in a file that already exists. A monitor started before the solver - which is the point of StartResultsMonitor, and what springDamperTutorial.py and 3SpringsDistance.py both do - therefore prints an error and exits at once. The docstring of StartResultsMonitor and docs/manual/resultsMonitor.md both say the file does not have to exist yet, which is false. The fix is to move the existence test into the waiting loop so that --wait 0 waits for the file to appear, and to decide what --wait N means for a file that never appears.
releaseNotes: MonitorResults waits for the file to appear, which its documentation had promised all along. WaitForData waits for the file, then for the header, then for the first row; the caller's existence test - which returned 'file not found' before any waiting could happen - now applies only to --once, which plots what exists and returns, so waiting there would be waiting for nothing. waitTimeout keeps its meaning and gains the file: 0, the default, waits without limit, which is what a monitor started before the solver needs, and N gives up after N seconds with a message naming the file. What is being waited for is announced, naming the file, because waiting forever for a file that will never appear is what a typo in the name looks like. So StartResultsMonitor works as its docstring says, and the two examples that start a monitor before the solver do what they show. Four tests, one of which writes the file from another thread after 0.4 s - the solver's part - and asserts that the monitor picked it up.
